       x1 13.44
       x2 13.39
       x3  1.02
correlation x1-x2 = 0.962

glossary.analogy_en: It is like tracking several plants: each plant starts at a different height, but you can still estimate the average weekly growth while allowing each plant its own starting point.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati kuyang'ana zomera zambiri: chilichonse chimayamba kutalika kosiyana, koma mumathabe kuyerekeza kukula kwamba pa sabata pamene malola chilichonse kukhala ndi poyambira chake.
glossary.application_en: Analysing repeated biomarker measurements from the same participants.
glossary.application_ny: Kusanthula ma biomarker obwerezabwereza kuchokera kwa omwewo.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112234)
rows = []
for pid in range(1, 41):
    intercept = rng.normal(12, 1.8)
    for week in [0, 4, 8]:
        rows.append((pid, week, intercept + 0.18*week +
                     rng.normal(0, 0.9)))
df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["id", "week", "value"])

fit = smf.mixedlm("value ~ week", df, groups=df["id"]).fit(reml=True)
print("fixed intercept =", round(float(fit.fe_params["Intercept"]), 3))
print("fixed week slope =", round(float(fit.fe_params["week"]), 3))
print("between-person variance =",
      round(float(fit.cov_re.iloc[0, 0]), 3))
print("within-person variance =", round(float(fit.scale), 3))
glossary.code_explanation_en: The fixed week slope is the average change over time. The random-effect variance describes how much participants differ in their baseline level; the residual variance describes within-person noise.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Slope ya week ndi kusintha kwamba pakapita nthawi. Random-effect variance ikufotokoza kusiyana kwa anthu pa poyambira; residual variance ikufotokoza phokoso mkati mwa munthu.
glossary.definition_en: Use for repeated or clustered continuous outcomes when observations within the same participant or site are correlated and you want both fixed effects and random variation between clusters.
glossary.explanation_ny: Munthu aliyense ali ndi poyambira payekha, kotero mizere yake siyodziyimira pawokha. Mixed model imapereka aliyense poyambira payekha pamene imayerekeza kusintha kwamba kwa nthawi. Gwiritsani ntchito pa zotsatira za manambala zobwerezabwereza kapena zogwirizana pamene deta ya munthu yemweyo kapena malo imodzi ili ndi ubale ndipo mukufuna fixed effects ndi kusiyana kwapakati pa magulu.
glossary.misconception_en: A random-intercept model assumes the same time slope for everyone; random slopes need more data. Convergence problems are common with few clusters.
glossary.misconception_ny: Random-intercept imaganizira kuti slope ya nthawi ndi yofanana kwa aliyense; random slopes zifuna deta yambiri. Mavuto a convergence amapezeka ngati magulu ndi ochepa.
glossary.output:
fixed intercept = 11.754
fixed week slope = 0.196
between-person variance = 1.98
within-person variance = 0.867

glossary.analogy_en: It is like surveying the same households repeatedly. You still want the city-wide average, but you must not count each household reply as fully independent evidence.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati kufunsa mabanja omwewo mobwerezabwereza. Mukufabe avareji ya mzinda wonse, koma simuyenera kuwerengera yankho lililonse ngati umboni wodziyimira pawokha.
glossary.application_en: Estimating population-average change in repeated test positivity.
glossary.application_ny: Kuyerekeza kusintha kwa kuchuluka kwa zotsatira zabwino mwa gulu lonse.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112235)
rows = []
for pid in range(1, 61):
    base = rng.normal(0, 0.6)
    for visit in [0, 1, 2]:
        group = pid % 2
        lin = -0.8 + base + 0.45*visit + 0.4*group
        prob = 1/(1+np.exp(-lin))
        rows.append((pid, visit, group, rng.binomial(1, prob)))
df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["id", "visit", "group", "event"])

gee = sm.GEE.from_formula("event ~ visit + group", groups="id",
                          data=df, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
for name in ["visit", "group"]:
    print(name, "log-OR =", round(float(gee.params[name]), 3),
          "p =", round(float(gee.pvalues[name]), 4))
print("n clusters =", df["id"].nunique())
glossary.code_explanation_en: GEE estimates a marginal, population-average log-odds ratio. Its SEs are wider than a naive logistic regression that treats each visit as independent.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: GEE imayerekeza log-odds ratio ya gulu lonse. Standard errors zake ndi zazikulu kuposa logistic regression yonamiza kuti ma visit ndi odziyimira pawokha.
glossary.definition_en: Use for repeated binary outcomes when your main interest is the population-average effect and you need standard errors that account for within-person correlation.
glossary.explanation_ny: GEE imazindikira kuti munthu yemweyo amapereka deta kangapo. Imasintha standard errors kuti zisakhale zazing'ono mwangozi, koma imayang'ana zotsatira za gulu lonse osati za munthu aliyense. Gwiritsani ntchito pa zotsatira za binary zobwerezabwereza pamene chidwi chachikulu ndi zotsatira za gulu lonse ndipo mukufuna standard errors zomwe ziganizira ubale wa mkati mwa munthu.
glossary.misconception_en: GEE needs enough clusters for reliable SEs. It is less efficient than a correctly specified mixed model.
glossary.misconception_ny: GEE ifuna magulu okwanira kuti SE zikhale zodalirika. Si yamphamvu ngati mixed model yoyenerera.
glossary.output:
visit log-OR = 0.379 p = 0.0315
group log-OR = 0.506 p = 0.132
n clusters = 60
glossary.term_ny: GEE ya zotsatira za binary zogwirizana

glossary.analogy_en: Following light bulbs until each fails, while some bulbs are still working when the study ends. Those still working do not count as failures, but their observed working time still contributes.
glossary.analogy_ny: Kutsata mababu mpaka awonongeke, pamene ena akadagwira ntchito kafukufuku akatha. Omwe akadagwira ntchito sawerengedwa kuti awonongeka, koma nthawi yawo yogwira ntchito imathandizira.
glossary.application_en: Time from treatment start to relapse, from birth to a neonatal outcome, or from device insertion to failure.
glossary.application_ny: Nthawi kuchokera pachiyambi cha chithandizo mpaka matenda abwerera, kuchokera pakubadwa mpaka zotsatira za makanda, kapena kuchokera kuikidwa kwa chida mpaka chawonongeka.
glossary.code_explanation_en: No standalone code is needed for this umbrella term. The Kaplan-Meier entry uses SurvfuncRight for the event-free curve; the Cox entry uses PHReg for adjusted hazard ratios.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Mawu akuluwa safuna code payokha. Cholemba cha Kaplan-Meier chimagwiritsa ntchito SurvfuncRight pa mphepete yopanda chochitika; cholemba cha Cox chimagwiritsa ntchito PHReg pa ma hazard ratio osinthidwa.
glossary.definition_en: Survival analysis is the set of methods for analysing time-to-event data, where the outcome is the time until an event and some subjects may be censored before that event is observed.
glossary.explanation_ny: Survival analysis siyongotanthauza imfa. Imaphunzira nthawi kuyambira poyambira mpaka chochitika, monga kutuluka m'chipatala kapena kuyambiranso kwa matenda. Anthu omwe sanachitike chochitika mpaka kafukufuku utha amadziwika kuti censored.
glossary.misconception_en: Ignoring censoring, or treating censored subjects as event-free forever, biases the estimate. A survival curve alone is not a causal effect, and competing events need explicit methods.
glossary.misconception_ny: Kunyalanyaza kutayika kwa deta, kapena kuona omwe atayika ngati opanda chochitika mpaka kalekale, kumakondera zotsatira. Mphepete yokha si zotsatira za causality, ndipo zochitika zopikisana zifunika njira zapadera.

glossary.analogy_en: It is like tracking how many runners are still uninjured at each mile, while allowing that some runners leave the study for reasons unrelated to injury.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati kuyang'ana othamanga angati omwe alibe kuvulala pa mailo iliyonse, ndikuvomereza kuti ena amachoka mu kafukufuku pazifukwa zosagwirizana ndi kuvulala.
glossary.application_en: Estimating event-free survival after a defined starting time.
glossary.application_ny: Kuyerekeza kukhala popanda chochitika pambuyo pa poyambira pomveka.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from statsmodels.duration.survfunc import SurvfuncRight

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112236)
n = 160
event_time = rng.exponential(scale=12, size=n)
censor_time = rng.uniform(3, 18, size=n)
duration = np.minimum(event_time, censor_time)
event = (event_time <= censor_time).astype(int)
df = pd.DataFrame({"duration": duration, "event": event})

sf = SurvfuncRight(df["duration"], df["event"])
print("participants =", len(df), "events =", int(df["event"].sum()))
for month in [3, 6, 12]:
    idx = max(0, int(np.searchsorted(sf.surv_times, month,
                                     side="right")) - 1)
    print("survival at month", month, "=",
          round(float(sf.surv_prob[idx]), 3))
glossary.code_explanation_en: The curve drops only at observed event times; censored participants contribute until their last known time. The printed values are the estimated proportions still event-free at 3, 6 and 12 months in this simulated cohort.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Mphepete imatsika pokhapo pa nthawi zomwe chochitika chinachitika; omwe atayika amathandizira mpaka nthawi yawo yomaliza yodziwika. Manambala osindikizidwa ndi gawo loyerekeza lopanda chochitika pa miyezi 3, 6 ndi 12 mu gulu lopangidwali.
glossary.definition_en: Use to estimate the probability of remaining event-free over time when some participants are censored before the event occurs.
glossary.explanation_ny: Kaplan-Meier imayesa kuti ndi gawo liti la anthu omwe akadali popanda chochitika pa nthawi iliyonse. Imalola anthu omwe atayika kutengapo mbali mpaka nthawi yomwe adaonekera komaliza. Gwiritsani ntchito kuyerekeza mwayi wokhalabe popanda chochitika pakapita nthawi pamene ena adatayika asanachitike chochitika.
glossary.misconception_en: A curve does not adjust for confounders and comparing curves informally can be misleading. Censoring that depends on prognosis biases the estimate.
glossary.misconception_ny: Mphepete silisinthidwa ndi zinthu zosokoneza ndipo kuyerekeza ma curve mwachisawawa kungasokeretse. Kutayika kogwirizana ndi chiopsezo kumakondera kuyerekezako.
glossary.output:
participants = 160 events = 86
survival at month 3 = 0.812
survival at month 6 = 0.634
survival at month 12 = 0.384

glossary.analogy_en: It is like comparing two groups' chances of a breakdown at any given mile of a journey, assuming one group's relative risk stays constant throughout the trip.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati kuyerekeza mwayi wakuti magulu awiri awonongeke pa mailo iliyonse ya ulendo, poganiza kuti kusiyana kwawo kumakhalabe kofanana pa ulendo wonse.
glossary.application_en: Modelling time to an event after adjustment for age and group.
glossary.application_ny: Kuyerekeza nthawi mpaka chochitika mutasintha zaka ndi gulu.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from statsmodels.duration.hazard_regression import PHReg

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112237)
n = 180
age = rng.normal(60, 8, n)
group = rng.integers(0, 2, n)
lp = 0.035*(age-60) + 0.55*group
event_time = rng.exponential(np.exp(-lp)*12)
censor_time = rng.uniform(3, 18, n)
duration = np.minimum(event_time, censor_time)
event = (event_time <= censor_time).astype(int)
df = pd.DataFrame({"duration": duration, "event": event,
                   "age": age, "group": group})

fit = PHReg(df["duration"], df[["age", "group"]],
            status=df["event"]).fit(disp=False)
for i, name in enumerate(["age", "group"]):
    print(name, "HR =", round(float(np.exp(fit.params[i])), 3),
          "p =", round(float(fit.pvalues[i]), 4))
print("events =", int(df["event"].sum()))
glossary.code_explanation_en: A hazard ratio above 1 means a higher instantaneous event rate at a given time, assuming proportional hazards. It is not a risk ratio or a survival-time ratio; the hazard is a rate, not a probability.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Hazard ratio woposa 1 ukutanthauza kuchuluka kwa zochitika pa nthawi inayake, ngati kuchuluka kwa ngozi kuli kofanana pakapita nthawi. Si risk ratio kapena chiŵerengero cha nthawi yopulumuka; hazard ndi mtengo, osati mwayi.
glossary.definition_en: Use for time-to-event outcomes when you want a hazard ratio for predictors while allowing the baseline hazard to remain unspecified.
glossary.explanation_ny: Cox imayerekeza kuti gulu lina lili ndi chiopsezo chachikulu bwanji chakumana ndi chochitika pa nthawi iliyonse. Simafuna kudziwa mawonekedwe enieni a chiopsekozo kwa nthawi yonse. Gwiritsani ntchito pa zotsatira za nthawi mpaka chochitika pamene mukufuna hazard ratio ya zinthu zolosera popanda kufotokoza mawonekedwe a baseline hazard.
glossary.misconception_en: If hazards are not proportional, a single HR can be misleading. Cox does not estimate the baseline survival curve without extra steps.
glossary.misconception_ny: Ngati kuchuluka kwa ngozi sikufanana pakapita nthawi, HR imodzi ikhoza kusokeretsa. Cox siyerekeza baseline survival popanda njira zina.
glossary.output:
age HR = 1.043 p = 0.0005
group HR = 1.652 p = 0.0092
events = 121

glossary.analogy_en: Two cars on the same road: the hazard ratio compares their instant-by-instant risk of a breakdown, assuming that relative risk stays constant throughout the journey.
glossary.analogy_ny: Magalimoto awiri panjira imodzi: hazard ratio uyerekeza chiopsezo chawo cha kuwonongeka pa nthawi iliyonse, poganiza kuti kusiyana kwawo kumakhalabe kofanana pa ulendo wonse.
glossary.application_en: Comparing time to relapse between treatment groups after adjusting for baseline prognosis.
glossary.application_ny: Kuyerekeza nthawi mpaka matenda abwerera pakati pa magulu a chithandizo mutasintha zinthu zoyambirira zokhudza zotsatira.
glossary.code_explanation_en: No standalone code is needed for this definition. In the Cox regression entry, exp(coefficient) produces each hazard ratio while the baseline hazard remains unspecified.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Apa palibe code payokha. Mu cholemba cha Cox regression, exp(coefficient) imapereka hazard ratio iliyonse pamene baseline hazard sinafotokozedwe.
glossary.definition_en: A hazard ratio is the ratio of two instantaneous event rates under a proportional-hazards model. It is usually obtained as exp(coefficient) from a Cox regression.
glossary.explanation_ny: Hazard ndi chiopsezo chachindunji chakumana ndi chochitika pa nthawi inayake, ngati munthu wafika pa nthawiyo popanda chochitika. Hazard ratio uyerekeza chiopsekochi pakati pa magulu awiri.
glossary.misconception_en: A hazard ratio is not a risk ratio, odds ratio or ratio of median survival times. If hazards change over time, one summary ratio can be misleading.
glossary.misconception_ny: Hazard ratio si risk ratio, odds ratio kapena chiŵerengero cha median survival. Ngati ma hazard asintha pakapita nthawi, chiŵerengero chimodzi chikhoza kusokeretsa.

glossary.analogy_en: It is like repeatedly drawing new handfuls from the same bag of beads to see how much the proportion of colours varies, without going back to the factory.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati kutenga mikono yatsopano mobwerezabwereza kuchokera m'thumba la mikanda kuti muone kuchuluka kwa mitundu kumasiyana bwanji, popanda kubwerera ku fakitale.
glossary.application_en: Estimating uncertainty for a skewed biomarker median when a formula is not convenient.
glossary.application_ny: Kuyerekeza kusatsimikizika kwa median ya biomarker wopendekerera pamene formula si yosavuta.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112238)
control = rng.lognormal(5.0, 0.6, 60)
treated = rng.lognormal(5.2, 0.6, 55)
observed = np.median(treated) - np.median(control)
B = 5000
boot = np.empty(B)
for i in range(B):
    bc = rng.choice(control, size=len(control), replace=True)
    bt = rng.choice(treated, size=len(treated), replace=True)
    boot[i] = np.median(bt) - np.median(bc)
lo, hi = np.percentile(boot, [2.5, 97.5])
print("observed median difference =", round(float(observed), 3))
print("bootstrap 95% percentile CI =", round(float(lo), 3),
      "to", round(float(hi), 3))
print("resamples =", B)
glossary.code_explanation_en: The interval is formed from the middle 95% of bootstrap statistics. It describes sampling uncertainty for this statistic under resampling.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Interval imapangidwa kuchokera pakati pa 95% ya ma statistic obwerezedwa. Imafotokoza kusatsimikizika kwa sample pa chiwerengerochi.
glossary.definition_en: Use when the sampling distribution of a statistic is awkward or you want a nonparametric interval without deriving a standard error formula.
glossary.explanation_ny: Bootstrap imatenga deta yomwe ilipo ndikuisankhanso mobwerezabwereza kuti iyonetse kuti chiwerengero chathu chingasinthike bwanji ngati tikanatenganso sample ina kuchokera ku gulu lomwelo. Gwiritsani ntchito pamene kagawidwe ka sample ka chiwerengero kuli kovuta kapena mukufuna interval popanda kupeza formula ya standard error.
glossary.misconception_en: Bootstrap fails with tiny samples, rare events, strong dependence or extreme statistics such as the maximum. Percentile intervals can be biased; BCa is an alternative.
glossary.misconception_ny: Bootstrap yalephera ndi ma sample ang'ono, zochitika zosowa, kudalirana kwakukulu kapena ziwerengero zapadera monga mtengo wapamwamba. Percentile interval ikhoza kukondera; BCa ndi njira ina.
glossary.output:
observed median difference = 50.381
bootstrap 95% percentile CI = -24.038 to 92.207
resamples = 5000

glossary.analogy_en: It is like a metal detector: sensitivity is how often it finds real metal, specificity is how often it stays quiet for harmless objects, and the threshold controls how beep-happy it is.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati chida chozindikira zitsulo: sensitivity ndi kuchuluka kwa zitsulo zenizeni zomwe chazipeza, specificity ndi kuchuluka kwa zinthu zopanda vuto zomwe chakhala chete, ndipo malire amalamulira kuchuluka kwa kubweep.
glossary.application_en: Evaluating a biomarker score for classifying a binary outcome.
glossary.application_ny: Kuwunika score ya biomarker pogawira zotsatira za binary.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_curve, auc, confusion_matrix

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112239)
y = np.r_[np.zeros(160, dtype=int), np.ones(140, dtype=int)]
score = np.r_[rng.normal(0.8, 0.5, 160), rng.normal(1.7, 0.6, 140)]

fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(y, score)
auc_value = auc(fpr, tpr)
j = tpr - fpr
best = int(np.argmax(j))
cut = thresholds[best]
pred = (score >= cut).astype(int)
tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred).ravel()
print("AUC =", round(float(auc_value), 3))
print("Youden J =", round(float(j[best]), 3))
print("candidate threshold =", round(float(cut), 3))
print("sensitivity =", round(tp/(tp+fn), 3),
      "specificity =", round(tn/(tn+fp), 3))
print("confusion matrix [[TN, FP], [FN, TP]] =",
      [[int(tn), int(fp)], [int(fn), int(tp)]])
glossary.code_explanation_en: AUC is the probability that a randomly chosen positive case scores above a randomly chosen negative case. Youden's J chooses the threshold maximising sensitivity plus specificity minus one.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: AUC ndi mwayi wakuti munthu wabwino asankhidwe ndi score yapamwamba kuposa munthu woipa. Youden's J imasankha malire omwe akulitsa sensitivity ndi specificity pamodzi.
glossary.definition_en: Use when a continuous marker or model score is used to discriminate between two groups and you want to summarise discrimination and examine a candidate cut-off.
glossary.explanation_ny: ROC imajambula kusinthanitsa pakati pa kuzindikira matenda (sensitivity) ndi kupewa chenjezo labodza (specificity). AUC imatiuza ngati score imasiyanitsa bwino; Youden ndi imodzi mwa njira zosankha malire. Gwiritsani ntchito pamene chiwerengero chosalekeza kapena model score chikugwiritsidwa ntchito kusiyanitsa magulu awiri ndipo mukufuna kufotokoza kusiyanitsa ndi kuyang'ana malire oti mugwiritse ntchito.
glossary.misconception_en: AUC ignores calibration and the clinical consequences of errors. A threshold tuned on the same data is optimistically biased.
glossary.misconception_ny: AUC sinyalanyaza kulinganiza kwa zolosera ndi zotsatira za zolakwika. Malire osinthidwa pa deta yomweyo amakhala otsika mtengo kwambiri.
glossary.output:
AUC = 0.901
Youden J = 0.658
candidate threshold = 1.133
sensitivity = 0.864 specificity = 0.794
confusion matrix [[TN, FP], [FN, TP]] = [[127, 33], [19, 121]]
glossary.term: ROC curve, AUC and Youden threshold
glossary.term_ny: ROC curve, AUC ndi Youden threshold

glossary.analogy_en: It is like practising several mock exams with different question sets, rather than memorising one practice paper and then sitting the same paper again.
glossary.analogy_ny: Zili ngati kuchita mayeso oyerekeza ambiri ndi mafunso osiyanasiyana, osati kukumbukira pepala limodzi la maphunziro kenako ndikuchitanso pepala lomwelo.
glossary.application_en: Estimating discrimination of a predictive model before external validation.
glossary.application_ny: Kuyerekeza kusiyanitsa kwa model yolosera musanatsimikiziridwe ndi deta yakunja.
glossary.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import RepeatedStratifiedKFold, cross_val_score

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112240)
n = 240
x1 = rng.normal(0, 1, n)
x2 = 0.5*x1 + rng.normal(0, 1, n)
y = (0.8*x1 - 0.4*x2 + rng.normal(0, 1, n) > 0).astype(int)
df = pd.DataFrame({"x1": x1, "x2": x2, "y": y})

pipe = Pipeline([("scale", StandardScaler()),
                 ("model", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))])
cv = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=3,
                             random_state=2026112240)
scores = cross_val_score(pipe, df[["x1", "x2"]], df["y"],
                         cv=cv, scoring="roc_auc")
print("folds =", len(scores))
print("mean CV AUC =", round(float(scores.mean()), 3))
print("SD across folds =", round(float(scores.std(ddof=1)), 3))
glossary.code_explanation_en: The mean is the estimated performance across repeated held-out folds; the SD shows variability. Because scaling and model fitting happen inside each fold, the estimate avoids leakage from using the full dataset's information.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Avareji ndi kagwiridwe koyerekeza pamagulu obisidwa obwerezabwereza; SD ikuwonetsa kusiyana. Popeza scaling ndi kuyika model zimachitika mkati mwa gulu lililonse, kuyerekezako kumapewa kutulutsa zidziwitso kuchokera ku deta yonse.
glossary.definition_en: Use to estimate how well a modelling pipeline generalises to new data when you cannot afford a separate large test set.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112241)
n = 220
x = rng.binomial(1, 0.5, n)
c = rng.normal(0, 1, n)
m = 0.6*x + 0.3*c + rng.normal(0, 0.8, n)
y = 0.4*m + 0.3*x + 0.2*c + rng.normal(0, 0.9, n)
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "m": m, "y": y, "c": c})

a = smf.ols("m ~ x + c", data=df).fit().params["x"]
b = smf.ols("y ~ m + x + c", data=df).fit().params["m"]
cp = smf.ols("y ~ x + c", data=df).fit().params["x"]
indirect = a*b
print("a path =", round(float(a), 3))
print("b path =", round(float(b), 3))
print("indirect effect a*b =", round(float(indirect), 3))
print("direct effect c-prime =", round(float(cp), 3))
print("total effect =", round(float(indirect + cp), 3))

glossary.code_explanation_ny: Gawo losadziwika ndi kuchulukitsa kwa njira ya exposure-mediator ndi mediator-zotsatira. Gawo lolunjika ndi ubale wa exposure wotsala pamene mediator wakhazikitsidwa.

Mwachitsanzo, maphunziro angakhudze ndalama, ndipo ndalama zikhudze thanzi. Gwiritsani ntchito pamene mukufuna kufunsa kuti gawo la zotsatira za exposure limadutsa pa chinthu chapakati, ndipo mutha kuteteza dongosolo ndi mfundo za causality.

glossary.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# SIMULATED TEACHING DATA — not real patient records.
rng = np.random.default_rng(2026112242)
n = 200
group = rng.integers(0, 2, n)
true_value = 10 + 1.5*group + rng.normal(0, 2, n)
observed = true_value.copy()
missing_prob = np.where(group == 1, 0.30, 0.10)
missing = rng.random(n) < missing_prob
observed[missing] = np.nan
df = pd.DataFrame({"group": group, "value": observed})

def diff_after_delta(delta):
    filled = df.copy()
    for g in [0, 1]:
        median_g = filled.loc[filled["group"] == g, "value"].median()
        mask = (filled["group"] == g) & filled["value"].isna()
        filled.loc[mask, "value"] = median_g + delta*g
    return filled.loc[filled["group"] == 1, "value"].mean() -            filled.loc[filled["group"] == 0, "value"].mean()

complete = df.dropna()
cc_diff = complete.loc[complete["group"] == 1, "value"].mean() - \
          complete.loc[complete["group"] == 0, "value"].mean()
print("missing rate by group =",
      df.groupby("group")["value"].apply(lambda s: round(s.isna().mean(), 3)).to_dict())
print("complete-case difference =", round(float(cc_diff), 3))
for delta in [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]:
    print("delta scenario", delta, "difference =",
          round(float(diff_after_delta(delta)), 3))
glossary.code_explanation_en: The complete-case estimate uses only participants with observed outcomes. Sensitivity scenarios shift imputed values in one group to explore how strong a missing-data bias would need to be to change the conclusion.
glossary.code_explanation_ny: Kuyerekeza kwa complete-case kugwiritsa ntchito omwe ali ndi zotsatira zowonedwa okha. Zochitika za sensitivity zimasintha ma value oyikidwa mu gulu limodzi kuti ziwone kukondera kofunika kusintha chigamulo.
glossary.definition_en: Use when conclusions may depend on how missing outcomes are handled, so you can show how the estimate changes under plausible assumptions rather than presenting one imputation as definitive.
glossary.explanation_ny: Deta ikasowa, kuyankha kumodzi kungakhale kokondera. Sensitivity analysis imatiwonetsa ngati chigamulochi chingasinthe pamene tipanga mfundo zosiyanasiyana zokhudza anthu omwe sanapereke deta. Gwiritsani ntchito pamene zotsatira zingadalire momwe deta yosowa yayendetsedwera, kuti muwonetse kuyerekezako kumasintha bwanji pansi pa mfundo zotheka osati kungopereka imputation imodzi ngati yotsimikizika.
glossary.misconception_en: Delta values are assumptions and must be justified from subject knowledge. This simple median fill does not preserve uncertainty or relationships among variables.
glossary.misconception_ny: Ma delta ndi mfundo zomwe ziyenera kutetezedwa ndi chidziwitso cha nkhani. Kudzaza ndi median sikusunga kusatsimikizika kapena ubale pakati pa zinthu.
